title: Sports Illustrated — At This Ultramarathon, There's No Finish Line (2019 race feature)
claims: Runners complete a 4.167-mile loop at the race organizer's home; after finishing one loop they rest, eat and use the port-a-potties until the next hour's start; failing to complete a loop before time elapses eliminates the runner, as does failing to appear on time for the next loop.
During daylight the runners follow a leafy dirt trail in the backyard; after dark the race moves to a road course for safety and returns to the backyard loop in the morning.
The race has no finite distance, no finish line and sudden-death elimination; it continues hour after hour through daylight, darkness, sun and rain while more than one runner remains.
To make the Big's field a runner must win one of the designated qualifiers or be hand-selected by Cantrell; the 2019 field came from more than 20 countries.
